speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether there are plans to increase the means-testing thresholds for annual values of properties (AVs) given that IRAS has revised the AVs upwards on 1 January 2023 to reflect the rise in market rents; and (b) why is the Ministry not using the AVs as of 2022 for the purpose of means-tested healthcare subsidies for households with zero per capita household income (PCHI).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Individuals who face difficulties in paying for their healthcare expenses due to a change in their AV under such circumstances, may approach their respective healthcare institution or provider for assistance.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljuned)
text: Can I confirm with the Senior Parliamentary Secretary that MOH has not been using the 2023 AVs for all its social support and means-testing?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljuned)
text: Alternatively, can MOH consider raising the AV threshold beyond $13,000 so that more Housing and Development Board (HDB) flat dwellers will not be excluded from the means-testing subsidies?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljuned)
text: Lastly, can I confirm that as long as a household is earning $1.00 or more, they are not subject to the AV criteria for the purpose of means-testing?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But I just wanted to confirm a few things.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On the Member's point of considering to remove this, this is a broader point that we are looking at.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As the Member would know, actually, there are also other subsidies and support which we offer to others who may be asset-rich but cash-poor, including non-means tested support in other schemes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And as I have mentioned earlier, if any of them are facing difficulties, they can always approach their healthcare providers and we will do our best to assist.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: So, can I just confirm with the Senior Parliamentary Secretary, for those residents who do not have a 2022 AV, how does MOH ensure that they are not worse off?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Can they appeal on the basis of their previous AV or something else that can be used as a proxy?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Will they still be subject to the AV criterion?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I think on the second question, there is going to be a cut-off somewhere.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But how we apply it is really about trying to assess and see if they do have needs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I do not think it is done in a manner that is unfair and draconian to the recipients.
